title: Bot Browser renamed to Card Browser / Download Cards / Cards Library
reality: v2.3.0 renamed **Bot Browser** to **Card Browser** throughout the UI, docs, onboarding, and Professor Mari guidance, and renamed **Browse Online** to **Download Cards**; the online browser was also unified with the Character/Persona/Agent library shell and now opens as **Cards Library** with a 'Browse character cards online' entry (2.3.0 Changed + Fixed). 2.3.1 further hardened Card Browser catalog requests against Undici identity/proxy MIME issues, and #3617 put Chub/CharacterTavern/Wyvern requests behind a shared safeFetch boundary.
fix: In the Import/Export section, replace 'all searchable from the in-app Bot Browser' with 'all searchable from the in-app Card Browser (renamed from Bot Browser in v2.3.0; the Browse Online action is now Download Cards, and the online browser opens inside the Cards Library shell shared with the Character/Persona/Agent libraries)'. Grep the rest of the skill file for any other 'Bot Browser' / 'Browse Online' occurrences and update them.

title: About Me AI drafting moved from per-editor AI Write to Professor Mari
reality: v2.3.2 (Changed) moved Conversation **About Me** drafting from per-editor **AI Write** controls to Professor Mari: the Character and Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings; Mari can inspect a saved character or persona, write the bio in that character's voice, and save it directly to the real About Me field. (v2.3.0 #3646 had first fixed the old AI Write path resolving {{user}} macros, but that whole per-editor flow was then replaced in 2.3.2.)
fix: Rewrite the `aboutMe` bullet in the Conversation-mode Profile section: remove the claim that it 'can be AI-written' via a 'gear-icon source picker' with `aboutMeSources` source settings in the card editor/popout. State instead that as of v2.3.2 AI drafting of About Me is done through Professor Mari (ask Mari; she inspects the saved character/persona, writes the bio in its voice, and saves it to the real About Me field), and that the editors no longer expose an AI Write model connection or source picker. Downgrade/annotate `aboutMeSources` (and DEFAULT_ABOUT_ME_SOURCES) as legacy schema fields no longer surfaced by the editor UI. Also add About Me drafting to the 'What Mari can actually do' list in the Professor Mari section.

title: Mari/app-data partial updates now preserve unrelated card fields (#3708)
reality: v2.3.2 (Fixed, #3708) preserved greetings, example dialogue, creator notes, system prompts, post-history instructions, character versions, and alternate greetings when Professor Mari or another app-data caller updates an unrelated Character Card field. Before this fix, a Mari `character.update` touching one field could silently wipe those other fields.
fix: In the Professor Mari section (near the `character.create`/`character.update` command discussion), add a note: as of v2.3.2 (#3708) Mari and other app-data callers performing partial card updates no longer clobber unrelated fields — first_mes/alternate_greetings, mes_example, creator_notes, system_prompt, post_history_instructions, and character versions survive an update to a different field; on earlier versions users should re-check these fields after any Mari-driven edit.

title: Sprite transparency: native-alpha-first pipeline undocumented
reality: v2.3.0 (Changed) reworked Character and Persona sprite transparency around a native-alpha-first pipeline: providers that cannot return transparent PNGs receive a subject-aware saturated chroma matte, then border-connected soft matting and color despill; the optional neural background remover is now reserved for genuinely complex backgrounds; saved legacy white-background sprites remain cleanable with restore points.
fix: In the Sprite System section, add a v2.3 paragraph describing the transparency pipeline: sprites prefer native alpha from the image provider; non-transparent providers get a chroma-matte + soft-matting + despill pass automatically; the neural remover is only used for complex backgrounds; legacy white-background sprites can still be cleaned, with restore points.

title: Character Metadata now has avatar upload/replace field above Name
reality: v2.3.3 (Fixed) added a clearly labeled avatar upload/replace field above Name in Character Metadata, reusing the same upload-and-crop flow as the editor portrait, discoverable on desktop and touch. The skill's description of the metadata identity block ('lead with a Title / comment field placed directly below Name') no longer describes the top of the block.
fix: Update the Character vs. Persona metadata paragraph (the Title/comment note): state that as of v2.3.3 the Character Metadata block starts with an avatar upload/replace field above Name (same upload/crop flow as the editor portrait), followed by Name and the Title/comment field.

title: Personas gained Open Full Library
reality: v2.3.0 (Added) gave Personas an **Open Full Library** with the same responsive card grid, search, sorting, preview pane, paging, scroll restoration, and editor return flow as the Character Library; v2.3.0 also switched both full libraries to the chroma text color from Settings.
fix: In the Character vs. Persona section (or a short UI note), add that Personas now have an Open Full Library (v2.3.0) mirroring the Character Library: card grid, search, sorting, preview pane, paging, and scroll restoration.

title: <START> example-dialogue separator survives XML sanitization (#3623)
reality: v2.3.0 (Fixed, #3623) preserved the standard `<START>` example-dialogue separator through XML prompt sanitization, including cards whose importer had already encoded the marker, while still escaping other XML-looking card text.
fix: In the schema/prompt discussion of `mes_example` (and/or the 'Writing examples' bullet in Common Mistakes), note that the conventional `<START>` separator between example exchanges is safe: since v2.3.0 (#3623) it survives XML prompt sanitization (even if a prior import encoded it), while other XML-like text in card fields is still escaped.

title: Prompt macros now resolved at final provider boundary (#3704)
reality: v2.3.2 (Fixed, #3704) resolved `{{user}}`, `{{char}}`, and other prompt macros in opening greetings and `/guided` instructions at the final provider boundary — including lorebook routing and embedding scans — so late prompt injections can no longer send raw identity placeholders to the model.
fix: In the Character vs. Persona section (where the skill says the engine substitutes `{{user}}` with the active persona), add that as of v2.3.2 (#3704) macro resolution happens at the final provider boundary: `{{user}}`/`{{char}}` in `first_mes`, alternate greetings, and `/guided` instructions are guaranteed resolved before the request leaves for the provider, including lorebook routing and embedding scans — card authors can safely use macros in greetings.

title: Character-panel filters became session-only in 2.3.3
reality: v2.3.3 (Fixed) reset stale Character-panel search, tag, favorite, and scroll filters during the update and made them session-only, so reopening Marinara shows the complete Character collection instead of an old filtered subset; Full Library sorting and position preferences are still persisted.
fix: Add a short note (Characters Panel / UI behavior context): since v2.3.3, Character-panel search/tag/favorite/scroll filters do not persist across app restarts (session-only); only Full Library sorting and position preferences persist. Useful when users report 'missing characters' — on <=2.3.2 a stale saved filter could hide the collection.

title: Mari card-generation fixes: blank turns and field-name normalization (#3674)
reality: v2.3.0 (Fixed, #3674) fixed Professor Mari returning blank character or lorebook generation turns, normalized common character-card field names, and made lorebook creation save generated entries atomically.
fix: In the Professor Mari section, add a brief v2.3.0 note (#3674): Mari no longer returns blank character-generation turns, common card field-name variants are normalized when she writes cards, and her lorebook creation saves entries atomically.
